 :J U D G M E N T:
This is a claim petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- with interest for the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 26.03.2023.

The averments of the petition in brief is as follows:
On 26.03.2023 at about 8.15 p.m., petitioner was proceeding by riding motor cycle bearing No. KA.05.KS.0335 from Mallapura village towards Bengaluru side, on extreme left side of Kodihalli - Kanakapura road and when he reached near Kurupete,
Kodihalli - Kanakapura road, Kanakapura town & taluk, Ramanagara district, at that time, the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No. KA.42.F.1278 came to the extreme right side of the road, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the injured was shifted to General hospital,
Kanakapura.
After first aid treatment, as per the advise of doctors, he was shifted to Nimhans hospital followed by Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and also underwent surgery.

The petitioner has spent Rs.8,00,000/-
towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishing food etc.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was aged about 26 years and was doing Management Information System work and earning Rs.27,000/- per month.
Due to injuries sustained by him, he is unable to do any work and lost his earning capacity.
The accident in question was occurred solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No. KA.42.F.1278.
The Kanakapura Police have registered a case against the said driver for the offences punishable U/Sec. 279 and 338 of IPC.

The respondent is the R.C.
owner and insurer of the bus.
Hence, the respondent is solely liable to pay the compensation.
With these averments petitioner prayed to award compensation.
3. In response to the notice issued by the Tribunal, the respondent appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.

4. The written statement averments of the respondent are hereunder:
The respondent has denied the cause and manner of accident, injuries sustained by the petitioner and also amount spent towards medical expenses.

Further contended that, as on the date and time of the alleged accident, the bus in question was on its schedule trip from Kanakapura via Sangama - Madivala and when the bus reached near Kurupete, Kanakapura town, the petitioner ridden his motor cycle from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and himself dashed against the front portion of the bus and caused the accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive, exorbitant, unreasonable and speculative in nature.
With these contentions, respondent prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:

sentences.text:
Whether the petitioner proves that, on 26.03.2023 at about 8.15 p.m, while he was riding motor cycle bearing Reg No. KA.05.KS.0335 near Kurupete, Kodihalli - Kanakapura road, Kanakapura taluk, Ramangara district, he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident due to rash or negligent driving of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No. KA.42.F.1278 by its driver as stated in the petition ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the reliefs sought for?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.22.
Further, Dr. Nagaraj B N, Orthopedic surgeon at SOADS hospital got examined as PW.2 and marked the documents at Ex.P23 & Ex.P24.
P.W.1 & P.W.2 were cross-examined from the side of respondent.
Per contra, the driver of KSRTC Bus examined himself as R.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R1 to Ex.R8.
R.W.1 was cross-examined from the side of petitioner.
7. Heard the arguments from both side.
Perused the records placed before the Tribunal.

The findings of this Tribunal to the above referred Issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 :- In the Affirmative.

Issue No.2 :- In the Partly Affirmative Issue No.3 :- As per the final order for the following:
:REASONS:
8. ISSUE No.1:-

Before going to discuss the issue No.1, it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".
Therefore, it is crystal clear that the petitioner has to prove his case on the principle of preponderance of probabilities.
9. In order to prove the case of petitioner, he has examined himself as P.W.1 by way of filing affidavit in support of his oral examination-in-chief.
Hence, this Tribunal need not to recapitulate the same once again at this juncture.
In order to prove issue No.1, P.W.1 has relied on Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8.
Accordingly, Ex.P.1 is the true copy of FIR.
Ex. P.2
is the true copy of complaint.

is the true copy of spot mahazar
Ex.P.4 is the true copy of spot sketch.
Ex.P.5 is the true copy of vehicle seizure mahazar.

is the true copy of IMV report.
Ex.P.7 is the true copy of wound certificate.

3 the true copy of charge sheet.

sentences.text: According to the respondent, as on the date and time of the alleged accident, the bus in question was on its schedule trip from Kanakapura via Sangama - Madivala and when the bus reached near Kurupete, Kanakapura town, the petitioner ridden his motor cycle from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and himself dashed against the front portion of the bus and caused the accident.
In order to substantiate the same, respondent has examined the driver of the bus as RW.1.
RW.1 was cross examined by the learned counsel for petitioner.
11. In the instant case, the petitioner has produced police documents.
As per Ex.P.2, complaint was lodged before the Kanakapura Traffic Police Station.
Thereafter, as per Ex.P.1, FIR was lodged against the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No. KA.42.F.1278.
Later the investigating officer has conducted spot mahazar and drawn spot sketch as per Ex.P3 & Ex.P4.
On careful perusal of Ex.P4 i.e., spot sketch, it appears to this tribunal that accident took place on the left side of the road which leads to Kodihalli to Kanakapura.
Further, the sketch reveals that the KSRTC Bus was coming from Kanakapura side to Kodihalli side.
As such, it is crystal clear that, the driver of Bus has came to the right side of the road and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner.
12. Further on perusal of Ex.P6, IMV report, both the vehicles have got damaged on their front right portion.

Further, on perusal of Ex.P.8, it appears to this Tribunal that, on the basis of complaint, the police have registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle and Investigating officer has submitted Charge sheet as per Ex.P.8 for the offences punishable U/Sec.279, 337 & 338 of IPC after completing investigation.
13. A careful perusal of Ex.P.7-wound certificate, it clearly goes to show that, petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.

Further, on perusal of Ex.P.8 i.e., charge sheet,
it reveals that, the driver of offending vehicle i.e., KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No. KA.42.F.1278 has been arrayed as an accused.
14. At the cost of repetition as per Ex.P8 viz. charge sheet, it reveals that the driver of KSRTC Bus has been arrayed as an accused.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Ranjith and another Vs.
Abdul Kayam Nab and another held that, "once a charge sheet has been filed and the driver has been held negligent, no further evidence is required to prove that the bus was being negligently driven by the bus driver.

entities.text:
Ranjith and another Vs.
Abdul Kayam Nab and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even if the eye witnesses are not examined, that will not be fatal to prove the death of the deceased due to negligence of the driver''.

15. Further, it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493, between Mallamma Vs. Balaji and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder: " Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold that, the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to prove the same".

At the cost of repetition, on careful perusal of Ex.P4 i.e.,
spot sketch, it appears to this tribunal that accident took place on the left side of the road which leads to Kodihalli to Kanakapura.
Further, the sketch reveals that the KSRTC Bus was coming from Kanakapura side to Kodihalli side.

As such, it is crystal clear that, the driver of Bus has came to the Arun K vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141016388/
4 right side of the road and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
16. ISSUE No.2:-
Already this Tribunal has observed that, the accident was caused due to the rash or negligent driving of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No. KA.42.F.1278.

It is needless to mention that,
respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
17. Age:- According to the petitioner, he was aged about 26 years as on the date of accident.
In order to substantiate the same, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.18 & Ex.P19 i.e., the notarized copies of his DL & Aadhaar Card.
These documents discloses the date of birth of petitioner as 02.10.1997.
The accident was occurred on 26.03.2023.
Hence, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 25 years and 05 months.

Therefore, by relying on the judgment of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA 5353/2024 (MV-D) decided on 07th August 2025 between The Managing Director, Motor Claims Hub BMTC, Shanthinagar, Bengaluru Vs. Smt. Jyothi and others, this tribunal considered the completed age of petitioner.
Accordingly, the age of the petitioner is considered as 25 years as on the date of accident.
18. Income:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he was working as management information system at Emergent Technix private Limited and earning a sum of Rs.27,000/- per month.
Per-contra, the respondent has denied the income of petitioner.
To substantiate his income the petitioner has produced Ex.P15, Ex.P.20 & Ex.P21.
Ex.P15 is the bank statement pertaining to the petitioner.
It reveals that, Prompt Personnel Company has credited the salary up to 31.01.2023.
Further on 16.05.2023, they have credited Rs.21,529/-.
That apart there is no entry regarding whether Emergent Technix Pvt. Ltd., has credited the salary.
Further it is relevant to note that as per Ex.P20, on 17.02.2023 Emergent Technix Pvt Ltd., has issued a offer letter in favour of the petitioner.
However, the petitioner has not examined any person of the said company and he has not produced any joining letter, salary slip.
In other words, petitioner has not produced the joining letter regarding whether he has joined Emergent Technix Pvt Ltd.
Or not.
Therefore, Ex.P20 will not come to the aid of petitioner to ascertain the exact salary of the petitioner as on the date of accident.

19. At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in a case of Godabai and others Vs. Goudappa and another reported in 2024 SCC Online KAR 15570 (Decided in MFA No. 201022/2018 ( MV-D) on 04.06.2024) wherein the Hon'ble Division Bench of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that at para 18 is as here under: "In the absence of any evidence or proof of income, the notional income has to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority''.

That apart, the Hon'ble High Court in M.F.A. No.101144 of 2020 ( MV-I) on 05.07.2023, between Ananda Vs. Arun and Another,
wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Para 9 (b) as hereunder:
" In the absence of any cogent material on record, it is for the courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess Arun K vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141016388/

sentences.text: the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant".
20. In the absence of examination of employer, the version of petitioner regarding income is not acceptable and this tribunal is declined to consider the income mentioned in Ex.P20.
As such the notional income of the petitioner is to be considered by relying on the judgments of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2022 is Rs.15,500/- per month.
It is pertinent to note that, the accident took place on 26.03.2023.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/- per month by adopting the method of Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
21. Loss of Future Income due to disability:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has averred that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident.
In order to substantiate the same the petitioner has produced wound certificate and discharge summary, which have been marked as Ex.P.7, Ex.P9 and Ex.P.10.
On perusal of these documents, it reveals that, the petitioner has sustained injuries.

It is relevant to mention that, respondent has disputed the injuries caused to P.W.1.
22.
The petitioner in order to prove the disability suffered by him, has examined the witness namely Dr. Nagaraj B N as P.W.2.
P.W2 has filed affidavit by way of examination-in-chief and produced 2 documents, which have been marked as Ex.P.23 and Ex.P.24.

PW.2 has stated in his affidavit that,
the petitioner has sustained fracture of the right femur, 4 th & 5th metacarpal fracture of the right hand, pelvis fracture with right SI joint instability with fracture of the posterior iliac spine with left acetabular lip fracture, blunt injury of the abdomen with contusion in liver & right kidney, right brachial plexus injury, traumatic epidural haemotoma with minimal cord compression and also underwent surgery.

Further, he has deposed that, the petitioner came for disability assessment on 18.06.2024 and complains of unable to walk normally, unable to sit down, squat and sit cross leg and unable to do any work in the right hand.
Finally P.W.2 has assessed the permanent disability of right upper limb at 87%, right lower limb at 47% and 40% for the whole body.
Further PW.2 was cross-examined from the side of respondent.
During the course of cross-examination, he has deposed that, he is not the treated doctor and only assessed the disability.

23. On perusal of the discharge summary of petitioner and evidence of medical witness coupled with wound certificate clearly reveals that, petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and suffered physical deformity.
Further, in the affidavit of PW.2 itself stated that, as per the recent X-ray, the fractures with respect to pelvis and right femur have been united with implant in situ.
Further, the evidence of PW.2 clearly reveals that he has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability.
By considering the avocation of petitioner, his age and injuries, the disability assessed by the P.W.2 is on higher side.
Hence, this Tribunal is considered the functional disability of the petitioner as 15% to the whole body.

sentences.text: As discussed supra, age of the injured is considered as 25 years and his income is considered as Rs.16,000/- per month.
Annual income comes to Rs.1,92,000/- (16,000 x 12).

Hence, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of injured as per Sarala Verma case is 18.
25.
If we multiplied yearly income with proper multiplier (1,92,000/- x 18), then it comes to Rs.34,56,000/-.
Already this Tribunal has considered the disability of petitioner as 15% to the whole body.
The same amount of Rs.5,18,400/- is awarded to the Injured/Petitioner under the head of loss of Future Income due to disability.
26. Medical Expenses:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he has incurred some amount towards medical expenses, transportation, food and conveyance.

In order to substantiate the incurring of medical expenses, the petitioner has produced medical bills which have marked as Ex.P.12 amounting to Rs.6,09,825/- which are supported with medical prescriptions, which have marked as Ex.P.13.

After careful perusal of the medical bills, this Tribunal is of the opinion that,
petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,09,825/- towards medical expenses.
27. Pain and suffering:-
According to the petitioner, due to accidental injuries, he has sustained physical deformity and he could not resume his avocation.

Further P.W.1 has stated that, he took treatment as an inpatient at Vasavi hospital from 30.03.2023 to 10.04.2023 for a period of 12 days and also at Bhagawan Mahaveer Jain hospital from 12.06.2023 to 14.06.2023 for a period of 03 days, in total the petitioner has taken 15 days treatment and has sustained fracture of mid shaft right femur, 4th & 5th metacarpal fracture of the right hand, tiles type C2 fracture pelvis, blunt trauma abdomen with contusion in liver and right kidney and right renal vein infract, right brachial plexus injury, traumatic epidural haemotoma, cervical cord syrinx chiari and minimal cord compression.

As per medical records and evidence of P.W.2 coupled with Ex.P.9, it appears to this Tribunal that,
the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient for a period of 15 days.
Further as per the evidence of doctor and medical records, it appears to this tribunal that, the petitioner has sustained physical deformity.
There is no serious dispute with regard to inpatient for 15 days.
As such, the petitioner has suffered a lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects, the Tribunal award compensation of Rs.75,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

28. Loss of income during the laidup period:-
The petitioner has produced discharge summary and same has been marked as Ex.P.9 & Ex.P10.

On perusal of these documents, it appears to this Tribunal that, the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient at Vasavi hospital from 30.03.2023 to 10.04.2023 and also at Bhagawan Mahaveer Jain hospital from 12.06.2023 to 14.06.2023 for a period of 15 days.
Naturally it shows that, he might have taken at least two and half months rest because of the injuries.
He has averred that, he was working as a MIS and earning Rs.27,000/- p.m.
This Tribunal has already considered the notional income of petitioner as Rs.16,000/- per month.

Hence, two and half Arun K vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141016388/
7 months is to be considered as loss of income during laid up period.

sentences.text: Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.40,000/- as compensation under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
29. Food, Nourishment and Attendant charges:-
In so for as food, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges are concerned, the petitioner has taken treatment as in patient for about 15 days.
The petitioner has not produced any documents in this regard.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and the period of treatment taken by the petitioner, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of Food, Nourishment and Attendant charges.
30. Loss of future amenities and happiness:-
The petitioner was aged about 25 years at the time of accident.
The petitioner has to live the rest of his life with physical deformity.
Therefore, he might have suffered pain, discomforts in life and loss of amenities.
By considering the age, nature of injuries, percentage of disability, Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.
31. Future medical expenses:-
PW.2 has stated that petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant and the estimation of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
As per the evidence of PW.2, the implants with respect to pelvis and femur are not removed.
Hence, by considering the future treatment and evidence of P.W.2, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards future medical expenses.

Attendant charges  6. Loss of future amenities and Rs. 25,000/-
 happiness.
 7. Towards future medical Rs. 40,000/-
 expenses.
 Total.

Rs. 13,38,225/-

33.
Regarding liability and interest.
The driver of the offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No. KA.42.F.1278 is the employee under respondent.
Therefore, respondent being employer of R.W.1 shall pay compensation to the petitioner.
Interest:

In view of the decision reported in MFA NO: 30131-2019 dtd, 12.5.2020 and M.F.A.No.100090/2014 C/w M.F.A.No.25107/2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and Others Vs.

34. ISSUE No.3:- In view of discussions made above, I proceed to pass the following.
:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the petition.

Petitioner is awarded just and  reasonable compensation of Rs.
 13,38,225/- (Rupees Thirteen lakhs thirty eight thousand two hundred and twenty five only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (except on the amount awarded under the head of future medical expenses)
from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the Tribunal.
Respondent shall deposit the compensation in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award Accordingly.

:APPORTIONMENT:
Out of the compensation amount, 80% of share of petitioner with interest is to be paid to him through E-payment, after due identification as per rules and after verifying the stay order from the Hon'ble Appellate Court, and the remaining 20% of his share with interest shall be invested in F.D. in his name in any nationalized bank for a period of 3 years.

This is a claim petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- with interest for the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 26.03.2023.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Due to the said impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, the injured was shifted to General hospital,
Kanakapura.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was aged about 26 years and was doing Management Information System work and earning Rs.27,000/- per month.
Due to injuries sustained by him, he is unable to do any work and lost his earning capacity.
The accident in question was occurred solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No. KA.42.F.1278.
The Kanakapura Police have registered a case against the said driver for the offences punishable U/Sec. 279 and 338 of IPC.
The respondent is the R.C.
owner and insurer of the bus.
Hence, the respondent is solely liable to pay the compensation.
With these averments petitioner prayed to award compensation.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive, exorbitant, unreasonable and speculative in nature.
opennyai_summary.issue:
5. On the basis of the above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:
:ISSUES:
Arun K vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141016388/
2 1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, on 26.03.2023 at about 8.15 p.m, while he was riding motor cycle bearing Reg No. KA.05.KS.0335 near Kurupete, Kodihalli - Kanakapura road, Kanakapura taluk, Ramangara district, he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident due to rash or negligent driving of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No. KA.42.F.1278 by its driver as stated in the petition ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the reliefs sought for?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Therefore, it is crystal clear that the petitioner has to prove his case on the principle of preponderance of probabilities.
Further, on perusal of Ex.P.8, it appears to this Tribunal that, on the basis of complaint, the police have registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle and Investigating officer has submitted Charge sheet as per Ex.P.8 for the offences punishable U/Sec.279, 337 & 338 of IPC after completing investigation.
13. A careful perusal of Ex.P.7-wound certificate, it clearly goes to show that, petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Ranjith and another Vs.
Abdul Kayam Nab and another held that, "once a charge sheet has been filed and the driver has been held negligent, no further evidence is required to prove that the bus was being negligently driven by the bus driver.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
The accident was occurred on 26.03.2023.
Hence, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 25 years and 05 months.
Therefore, by relying on the judgment of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA 5353/2024 (MV-D) decided on 07th August 2025 between The Managing Director, Motor Claims Hub BMTC, Shanthinagar, Bengaluru Vs. Smt. Jyothi and others, this tribunal considered the completed age of petitioner.
Accordingly, the age of the petitioner is considered as 25 years as on the date of accident.
In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he was working as management information system at Emergent Technix private Limited and earning a sum of Rs.27,000/- per month.
However, the petitioner has not examined any person of the said company and he has not produced any joining letter, salary slip.
Therefore, Ex.P20 will not come to the aid of petitioner to ascertain the exact salary of the petitioner as on the date of accident.
20. In the absence of examination of employer, the version of petitioner regarding income is not acceptable and this tribunal is declined to consider the income mentioned in Ex.P20.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/- per month by adopting the method of Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
21. Loss of Future Income due to disability:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has averred that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident.
On perusal of these documents, it reveals that, the petitioner has sustained injuries.
Further, the evidence of PW.2 clearly reveals that he has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability.
Hence, this Tribunal is considered the functional disability of the petitioner as 15% to the whole body.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.40,000/- as compensation under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and the period of treatment taken by the petitioner, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of Food, Nourishment and Attendant charges.
The petitioner has to live the rest of his life with physical deformity.
By considering the age, nature of injuries, percentage of disability, Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.
31. Future medical expenses:-
As per the evidence of PW.2, the implants with respect to pelvis and femur are not removed.
Hence, by considering the future treatment and evidence of P.W.2, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards future medical expenses.
32. Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Heads Amount  1.Towards loss of Future income.
Rs. 5,18,400 /-
 2. Towards Medical Expenses.
Rs. 75,000/-
 4. Loss of income during the laid  up period Rs. 40,000/-
5 . Food, Nourishment and Rs. 30,000/-
Attendant charges  6. Loss of future amenities and Rs. 25,000/-
 happiness.
 7. Towards future medical Rs. 40,000/-
 expenses.
 Total.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for just and reasonable amount of Rs. 13,38,225/-.
33.
Therefore, respondent being employer of R.W.1 shall pay compensation to the petitioner.
Interest:
, rate of interest on the compensation amount is awarded at 6% p.a. (except on the amount awarded under the head of future medical expenses) from the date of petition.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the Partly Affirmative.
34. ISSUE No.3:- In view of discussions made above, I proceed to pass the following.
:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the petition.
Petitioner is awarded just and  reasonable compensation of Rs.
 13,38,225/- (Rupees Thirteen lakhs thirty eight thousand two hundred and twenty five only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (except on the amount awarded under the head of future medical expenses)
from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the Tribunal.
Respondent shall deposit the compensation in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award Accordingly.
:APPORTIONMENT:
Out of the compensation amount, 80% of share of petitioner with interest is to be paid to him through E-payment, after due identification as per rules and after verifying the stay order from the Hon'ble Appellate Court, and the remaining 20% of his share with interest shall be invested in F.D. in his name in any nationalized bank for a period of 3 years.
